THE IDEA & METHOD

Plan media around the life
happening around it.

AI-Native pDOOH World-Model connects a person's encounter with a screen to budget allocation across an inventory. It combines screen coordinates, local context, representative audiences, and road-network mobility in a spatially grounded simulation workflow.

A language model proposes individual behavioral policies; a local simulator evolves them over 24 hours. Viewing opportunities and creative-response evidence then inform screen scores, share-of-time allocations, and campaign-period cost estimates.

A city-to-campaign pipeline.

Four connected stages carry evidence from the original screen record to the final quote.

◎

Ground the inventory

Resolve coordinates, inspect streets and venues, and retain the original screen identifier.

Screen + location + context
◇

Define the campaign

Set the creative, budget, period, currency, and media-buying constraints.

Creative + commercial inputs
⌁

Simulate the day

Generate representative policies, then evolve movement and screen encounters locally.

Hourly opportunity evidence
▥

Allocate investment

Compare objectives, assign a budget and SOT, then export a screen-level proposal.

Allocation + quote + provenance

A traceable planning scenario: where to invest, how much to allocate, and what evidence supports each decision.

SPATIALLY GROUNDED SIMULATION

The street is part of the model.

Screen location, movement, visibility, available attention, and repeat encounters shape the simulated opportunity to see.

Policies first. Local evolution next.

The fast mode generates one behavioral policy per synthetic representative, then runs the 24-hour evolution locally. The implementation batches 25 profiles per request with up to four policy-generation workers.

Opportunity is not conversion.

A screen encounter depends on geometry and an attention window. The policy models noticing, dwell, and curiosity. Creative favorability and interest are recorded separately; neither is treated as a purchase probability.

Attention policy

Context gates the encounter.

When line of sight exists and viewing time is positive, the policy applies a bounded attention probability. Otherwise, the encounter remains a pass-by.

pa,t=clip0,1(pa·min(1,τa,t5)1+fana,t+βaqa,t)

p: base notice probability · τ: available seconds · f: fatigue · n: previous encounters · βq: peer contribution. These are uncalibrated scenario parameters, not measured behavioral probabilities.

FROM SIMULATION TO A QUOTE

Every number has a denominator.

Keep the observed simulation window, campaign duration, and purchased share of time explicit.

Campaign impressions
I^s=Os·24Hs·D·αs

Os is the accumulated opportunity count over Hs simulated hours. D is the campaign length in days; αs is SOT. Repeated encounters count again.

Media investment
Bs≈I^s1000·cs·(1+δ)

cs is CPM after markup and currency conversion; δ is the DSP fee rate. Actual allocations are cent-based and capacity-constrained. The daily amount is Bs / D.

Allocation preference
ws∝uscs,all-in[1+λ(ng(s)−1)]

Objective-specific utility us is weighted against cost and regional concentration. A seed allocation precedes weighted redistribution under budget, per-screen, and inventory limits. This is a heuristic, not a global optimum.

Exposure efficiency
CPMplan=1000·∑Bs∑I^s

This is a cost-per-exposure measure. Financial ROI requires incremental revenue and margin evidence: ROI = (ΔR · m − C) / C, with total cost C including supplied execution costs.
